content: A comprehensive list of expanded indicators is provided in Appendix 1 and Appendix 2. Core indicators are deemed essential and represent the minimum set of metrics required to monitor trends and evaluate progress in implementing Integrated People-Centered Eye Care (IPEC) within each health information system domain. Expanded indicators can be selected and tailored to align with the specific objectives of a country’s eye care strategic plan. Additionally, the action plan includes core indicators for tracking progress in trachoma elimination. Roles and Responsibilities of Key Stakeholders: Member States: Address the population's needs for eye care and integrate eye care into health policies to ensure the provision of comprehensive, high-quality eye health services closer to where people live. Prevent catastrophic financial expenditures on eye care for individuals. Ensure the availability of sufficient and competent human resources at all levels of healthcare. Reorient the primary healthcare system and health workforce through task delegation and task sharing, ensuring equitable distribution and promoting rural retention of healthcare workers. Strengthen academic qualifications through competency-based training frameworks and advocate for the recognition of allied eye care health workers, including optometrists and ophthalmic technicians, as core members of the eye health workforce. Enhance eye health surveillance, data collection, analysis, and utilization for informed decision-making, advocacy, and course correction as needed. World Health Organization (WHO): Provide leadership, coordination, and guidance to Member States and partners in promoting and implementing IPEC. Develop and update technical and strategic guidance documents to support Member States in capacity building, formulating national strategy documents, and improving eye health literacy. Collaborate with global, regional, and national partners, including WHO collaborating centers, to establish capacity-building networks for training and research in eye health. Engage with non-state actors, including non-governmental organizations, civil society organizations, and the private sector, to foster collaboration and leverage partnerships for improving access to quality, comprehensive eye care. Partner with global technology and digital innovation hubs to harness the potential of digital innovation and leverage technology for equitable access to universal eye health. International Partners, Non-Governmental Organizations, Civil Society, and the Private Sector: Advocate for and commit to universal eye care. Collaborate with WHO, national governments, and other partners to promote and support universal eye health through strengthened primary healthcare. Utilize local presence and capacities to establish partnerships with governments, mobilize and share knowledge, provide eye care services, and amplify the voices of underserved and vulnerable populations. The private sector plays a critical role in driving innovation and expanding digital technologies to improve the availability and accessibility of affordable, effective, and high-quality eye care products and services. Monitoring and Evaluation: Core and expanded indicators are categorized into input, output, outcome, and impact metrics to monitor and evaluate progress toward IPEC implementation. Indicators include governance measures, such as the integration of eye care into national health plans, and financial risk protection for essential services like cataract surgery, optical devices, and diabetic retinopathy treatment. Eye care workforce density and distribution, availability of refractive and vision rehabilitation services, and waiting times for cataract surgery are also tracked. Effective coverage metrics, such as cataract surgical outcomes and refractive error correction, are emphasized to ensure quality service delivery. Data sources include routine health facility reports, government health and education ministry reports, and professional associations. This detailed framework ensures a systematic approach to improving eye health services globally, with a focus on equity, accessibility, and quality.
